statements.quote: make new Democrats before voter registration ends

statements.speaker: Joseph Kopser
statements.claim: Presents talking to Republican and independent voters as compatible with progressive values and representing the district.

statements.speaker: Liz Watson

statements.speaker: Dan Canon
statements.claim: Presents firsthand experience of economic insecurity as a qualification that conventional politicians may lack.

statements.speaker: Rob Chatlos
statements.claim: Presents his work as a truck driver and working-class identity as a source of connection with people outside typical political attention.

comparisons.analysis: Crowe emphasizes expanding the Democratic electorate through registration and mobilization; Kopser emphasizes winning Republican crossover voters. This compares their publicly stated electoral strategies, not which strategy would actually win.
Both present experience outside conventional politics as a reason to represent the district. The shared campaign frame does not establish identical policies or personal circumstances.

In the same reported opioid discussion, Canon specifies harm-reduction tools and Chatlos emphasizes securing resources. Funding and treatment approaches can coexist; neither is coded as opposing the other.
